title: A bioengineering method for modeling alveolar Rhabdomyosarcoma and assessing chemotherapy responses
author: Stefanek, Samiei, et al.
materials: The proposed 3D EM has a relatively simple fabrication method in comparison with existing 3D culture models, which require delicately arranging cell sheets [20], extrusion bioprinting [21], or decellularizing tissues [22]. Furthermore, the proposed EM's uniform geometry allows for even nutrient and media penetration and simplifies imaging in comparison to non-uniform constructs formed by pipetting hydrogels directly into well-plates [18]. The fabrication process of the proposed EM is highly reproducible which allows for direct comparisons if used in different studies. Despite the ease of fabrication, the collagen-I hydrogel still mimics the tumor ECM to a similar degree as existing studies which have used alginate/gelatin/fibrinogen composite hydrogels [21] or murine basement membrane extract [18].

steps.title: Fabricate PDMS molds
steps.instruction: Mix PDMS elastomer and curing agent at a 10:1 ratio, degas, pour to form a 1 mm layer, cure, cut, punch holes, sterilize, and place in a 12‑well plate.

substeps.instruction: Combine PDMS elastomer and curing agent in a 10:1 ratio as per manufacturer and mix thoroughly.
Degas the mixture in a vacuum chamber until no bubbles remain.
Pour the mixture over a glass slide, using aluminum foil or PDMS walls to contain it, and calculate volume to achieve a 1 mm thickness (e.g., a 50 × 75 mm slide requires 3.75 mL).
Cure the poured PDMS at 70 °C for 1–2 h (oven or hot‑plate).
Using a scalpel, cut the cured PDMS sheet into 15 mm squares.
Punch a 5 mm diameter hole in the centre of each square with a biopsy punch.
Sterilize the molds: autoclave at 120 °C, or if unavailable, incubate in 70 % ethanol for 1 h, rinse with 100 % ethanol, then dry in an oven at 70 °C for ≥6 h.
Store the sterile molds in a sealed container and, under aseptic conditions, transfer them to a 12‑well plate.

steps.title: Prepare 2D cell cultures
steps.instruction: Grow RH30 and C2C12 cells to 80 % confluence, detach with trypsin, and collect cells for downstream use.

substeps.instruction: Prepare complete media: RPMI‑1640 with 10 % FBS and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin (for RH30) and complete DMEM with the same supplements (for C2C12).
Culture RH30 cells in RPMI‑1640 and C2C12 cells in DMEM in T‑75 flasks until they reach ~80 % confluence.
Aspirate the spent media and wash each flask with 4 mL PBS or trypsin‑EDTA.
Add 5 mL trypsin‑EDTA to each flask and incubate 5 min in a 37 °C incubator; gently pipette to detach cells.
Transfer the cell suspension to a centrifuge tube and add 10 mL fresh complete media to dilute.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant; the cell pellet is ready for 3D culture or further 2D passaging.

steps.title: Create 3D collagen constructs
steps.instruction: Embed cells in a collagen‑I hydrogel, load into PDMS molds, crosslink, and culture.

substeps.instruction: Keep all collagen solutions and any reagents that will be mixed with collagen at 4 °C until crosslinking.
Resuspend the harvested RH30 cells in 1 mL chilled RPMI‑1640 and C2C12 cells in 1 mL chilled DMEM (both kept at 4 °C).
Dilute the collagen solution with the cell‑suspended media (and additional media if needed) to obtain a final cell density of 2 × 10⁶ cells/mL and a collagen concentration of 3 mg/mL.
If using PureCol EZ Gel (initially 5 mg/mL), no further adjustment is required because pH and ionic strength are pre‑adjusted.
If using an acidic collagen such as FibriCol, add appropriate volumes of 10× PBS, NaOH, and distilled water to reach 1× PBS ionic strength and pH 7.4 before mixing with cells.
Pipette 20 µL of the cell‑laden hydrogel into the centre of each 5 mm‑diameter PDMS mold cavity.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂ for 45 min to thermally crosslink the hydrogel.
Gently add 2 mL of the appropriate complete media to each well and culture for 12 h or overnight.
Add cytotoxic drugs or other experimental reagents as desired.
Monitor the constructs at relevant time points using bright‑field microscopy, live/dead viability assays, immunocytochemistry, or other analyses.

steps.title: Live/Dead viability staining
steps.instruction: Stain 3D constructs with calcein AM and ethidium homodimer‑1 and image.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a staining solution in DPBS containing 2 µM calcein AM and 4 µM ethidium homodimer‑1; for 10 mL use 5 µL calcein AM and 20 µL EthD‑1.
Remove media from each well and add enough live/dead solution to cover the construct.
Incubate in the dark at room temperature for 1–2 h.
Remove the staining solution and wash the constructs three times with DPBS, each wash lasting 5 min.
Immediately image the stained constructs using a confocal microscope.

steps.title: Immunocytochemistry of 3D constructs
steps.instruction: Fix, block, and stain constructs with primary and secondary antibodies, then image.

substeps.instruction: Remove media and fix cells with 3.7 % formaldehyde in DPBS at room temperature for 40 min.
Wash three times with DPBS, 5 min each wash.
Block for 2 h at room temperature with 5 % BSA and 0.3 % Triton‑X‑100.
Prepare primary‑antibody solutions at 1:300 dilution in DPBS containing 1 % BSA and 0.3 % Triton‑X‑100 (combine p62 and LC3 together; prepare PARP separately).
Incubate the samples overnight at room temperature with the appropriate primary‑antibody solution.
Wash three times with DPBS, 5 min each.
Prepare secondary‑antibody solutions at 1:300 dilution in DPBS with 1 % BSA and 0.3 % Triton‑X‑100 (separate solutions for each primary).
Incubate in the dark for 2–4 h at room temperature.
Remove secondary solution and incubate with DAPI solution for 1–2 h in the dark at room temperature.
Wash three times with DPBS, 5 min each.
Immediately image the stained samples using a confocal microscope.
